### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **3** package(s): `@objectstack/service-automation`, `@objectstack/service-job`, `@objectstack/trigger-schedule`, touching **40** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **3** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/services/service-automation/src/index.ts`, `packages/services/service-job/src/index.ts`, `packages/triggers/trigger-schedule/src/index.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**2** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/automation/flows.mdx`  _(via flowName (symbol, a field of interface MissedScheduledRun; a field of interface MissedScheduledRunInput))_
- `content/docs/automation/jobs.mdx`  _(via flowName (symbol, a field of interface MissedScheduledRun; a field of interface MissedScheduledRunInput))_

⛔ **5** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v16.mdx`  _(via AutomationEngine (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-0.mdx`  _(via AutomationEngine (symbol, a top-level class), flowName (symbol, a field of interface MissedScheduledRun; a field of interface MissedScheduledRunInput))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-5.mdx`  _(via flowName (symbol, a field of interface MissedScheduledRun; a field of interface MissedScheduledRunInput), timed_out (literal, a string literal in SysAutomationRun; a string literal in TERMINAL_RUN_STATUSES; a string literal in lifecycle))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-6.mdx`  _(via AutomationEngine (symbol, a top-level class))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **3** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/services/service-automation/src/index.ts`, `packages/services/service-job/src/index.ts`, `packages/triggers/trigger-schedule/src/index.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **8** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **55** of **207** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **7** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json d0a7e748a933a7fb549c38c3105c1c49f5935dec` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `2054eb0a6e884a0824a559f9e2f190c92ddaa023` — the merge of head `1bff9c7e9fc201d2593133e1c14ac19cf185b704` into base `d0a7e748a933a7fb549c38c3105c1c49f5935dec`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 2054eb0a6e884a0824a559f9e2f190c92ddaa023 && git checkout 2054eb0a6e884a0824a559f9e2f190c92ddaa023
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin d0a7e748a933a7fb549c38c3105c1c49f5935dec 1bff9c7e9fc201d2593133e1c14ac19cf185b704 && git checkout -B drift-repro d0a7e748a933a7fb549c38c3105c1c49f5935dec && git merge --no-ff 1bff9c7e9fc201d2593133e1c14ac19cf185b704

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json d0a7e748a933a7fb549c38c3105c1c49f5935dec
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs d0a7e748a933a7fb549c38c3105c1c49f5935dec` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `TIER_DEFAULT`
Head-sha: `1bff9c7e9fc201d2593133e1c14ac19cf185b704`
Local-runs: none

Inputs read: card #25235 (body and all 11 comments: claim `6353512245`, ruling `6353729816` letter A, hold `6354378101`, spec answer `6355021401`, unlock `6392088171`, claim `6433183891`, os-dev-report `6434107183`); PR #26485 body, its 15-file list, and the net diff `origin/main...1bff9c7e` (15 files, +1381/−13; merge base `68901b0383`); the head's check-runs at 2026-10-27T05:05Z. Face: `record-recognisers --paths` over the file list decides no face (no published schema, no governed path), so the changeset's `Clause-②: yes (widening)` line owes the declaration face, TIER_DEFAULT — the tier this record is served at.

### ① Derived judgments

Every accept-set and public-surface change the diff implies, each judged against the ruling (`6353729816`, items 2–9) and the cited code at the head:

1. **Stored vocabulary widens by one member.** `sys_automation_run.status` `Field.select` options gain `missed` (7 → 8 members), the retention `onlyWhen` set gains `missed`, and `TERMINAL_RUN_STATUSES` gains `missed` (engine.ts:1671) — the three sites the engine's own docblock says widen together, widened in the same change as the one producer. **Right.** The value is already the spec's: `ExecutionStatus` carries `'missed'` appended last at `packages/spec/src/automation/execution.zod.ts:53` (PR #25363, card #25325), so the stored column aligns to the protocol rather than widening past it (Prime Directive 12 holds; ADR-0078 condition met). `isTerminalRunStatus` (engine.ts:1677) reads the list, and the store's row gate (`suspended-run-store.ts:145`, `:841`, `:860`) reads that predicate, so a `missed` row is written and listed as history with no fourth copy. `plugin-approvals` `RUN_STATUS_LIVENESS` already carries `missed: 'terminal'` on `main` (approval-service.ts:572) and is typed `satisfies Record of ExecutionStatus to RunLiveness` — untouched, right. No exact-list pin outside the diff enumerates the old five (grepped the head's tests).
2. **Wire surface widens by construction, not by edit.** `listRuns(name, { status })` and `GET …/runs?status=` read the spec enum (`automation-api.zod.ts:692`, `runtime/src/domains/automation.ts:3829` `parseEnumParam('status', …, ExecutionStatus.options)`); the diff holds no `packages/runtime/**` or `packages/spec/**` path. **Right** (ruling item 9).
3. **`@objectstack/service-automation` public surface, all additive.** `AutomationEngine.recordMissedRun(missed)` answering a `MissedRunOutcome` promise and `AutomationEngine.missedRunLimit()` answering `number | null` (new public methods); `FlowTrigger.release?(flowName)` (optional member — an existing implementer compiles unchanged); `SuspendedRunStore.maxTerminalRunsPerFlow?: number` (optional readonly; the two store classes turn a `private readonly` field public, same name and value); barrel types `MissedScheduledRun`, `MissedRunOutcome`; `TerminalRunStatus` widens. `missedRunId()` is exported from `engine.ts` but the barrel exports by name (index.ts:4, :85–92) and does not re-export it — consistent with the PR body's surface list, which omits it. **Right**, widening only; nothing accepted before is refused.
4. **`@objectstack/service-job`:** `DbJobAdapter.readArming(name)` answering a `JobArming | null` promise (public method, adapter-local like `setReplayGuard`, ⛔ not on `IJobService` — as claimed and ruled); barrel type `JobArming`. A read that throws rejects, never answers "inactive" (pinned). **Right.**
5. **`@objectstack/trigger-schedule`:** `ScheduleTrigger.release(flowName)` public; `JobServiceSurface.readArming?`, `ScheduleDispatchLedger.recordMissedRun?`, `ScheduleDispatchLedger.missedRunLimit?` optional structural members; barrel types `JobArmingReading`, `MissedScheduledRunInput`; new module `missed-due-times.ts` (`dueTimesInSilence`, `DROPPED_DUE_TIME_COUNT_CEILING`, not barrel-exported). **Right**, widening only.
6. **The one existing-behaviour change: a refusal on purpose disarms by name.** `start()`'s three refusals (policy off, no schedule descriptor, missing organization) call `release()` instead of `stop()`, and the engine's scheduled-work policy gate (engine.ts:3692–3706) calls `trigger.release?.()` on every pass since that gate returns before `start()` is reached. `release()` cancels the job named `flow-schedule:` plus the flow name through the job service whether or not this process bound it; `DbJobAdapter.cancel` → `setActive(name, false)` (db-job-adapter.ts:321, :702). **Right** — this is exactly ruling item 6's fix, inside the claimed surface, with no `sys_job` column, `platform-objects` or spec change; pinned both ways (OFF kernel between two ON kernels: zero rows; evicted ON kernel: one row per due time).
7. **Gap bounds, as ruled (item 5c).** Start = `firstInstant(updated_at, last_run_at, created_at)`; at the head both `upsertJobRow` (:663) and `bumpJob` (:743) write `updated_at: now`, so `updated_at` is the newest instant a kernel touched the job, ≥ `last_run_at`, = bind time before any fire — the ruling's bound or tighter. End = this kernel's first BIND for the flow (ruling text says first tick; hold `6354378101` records why the due-time set is identical for cron and interval, and `dueTimesInSilence` is pinned to answer only instants that are the start of their own tick window, the ledger key). Read once per flow per kernel (`armingRead`), issued synchronously BEFORE `schedule()` rewrites the row; a late read can only lose a `missed` entry, never invent one. **Right.**
8. **Ledger verdict and the no-ledger skip (items 5c–d).** A due time is recorded only when the row is `active` AND `store.read(dispatchKey)` answers no claim; the key is `scheduleDispatchKey(flow, computeTickWindow(armedSchedule, due))`, the same function the handler claims with (schedule-trigger.ts:828). `missedRunLimit()` answers `null` when `flowDispatchStore` is null or has no `read` — the same condition under which `dispatch-claims.ts:82` says "IN-PROCESS ONLY" — and the trigger then warns once naming the flow and records nothing; a ledger read that throws answers `unverifiable`, nothing recorded. ⛔ Never inferred from an absent claim. **Right.**
9. **One row per (flow, due time) (item 5a).** `missedRunId` = `run_missed_` + flow name + `_` + due-time epoch ms; the store prefixes `run_` again (`HISTORY_PREFIX + runId`), so the durable id reads `run_run_missed_…` — deterministic and unique per (flow, due time), the two-replica pin holds one row. Cosmetic double prefix, not a contract point.
10. **Row shape (items 2, 5f).** `startedAt` = due time, `completedAt` = detection, `steps: []`, `trigger.type = 'schedule'`, `organizationId` from the flow's declared organization; `durationMs` is never set, `recordLog` (run-history.ts) passes `entry.durationMs` through, and the store writes `duration_ms: record.durationMs ?? null` — absent, as the spec TSDoc says; no `error`, no `refusalMessage`. **Right.**
11. **The bound (item 5e).** Per flow per detection, the newest `maxTerminalRunsPerFlow` due times as the store was configured (default 100), read through `missedRunLimit()`, no second literal for the record bound; oldest dropped first; one `warn` naming the flow, the count and the earliest dropped due time. Two readings beside the ruling's text, both judged right: (a) when the store declares no cap or `0` (cap disabled), the engine's existing `maxLogSize` (default 1000, engine.ts:834) is the bound rather than "unbounded" — an existing bound reused, not a new one; (b) `DROPPED_DUE_TIME_COUNT_CEILING = 1_000` is a new literal, but it bounds the WALK that counts dropped due times for the warn line (the line then says "at least 1000"), never what is recorded; the earliest dropped instant stays exact. Neither widens or narrows the ruled record bound.
12. **No replay (item 5b).** Nothing is dispatched for a missed due time; `d.ran` stays at its prior count in every two-kernel case; the next due time runs normally. `cloud#1288` untouched. **Right.**
13. **Nothing else in the diff** touches `packages/spec/**`, `packages/platform-objects/**`, `packages/runtime/**`, `packages/client`, a gate or a script (item 9) — verified on the 15-path file list.

### ② Semver level

Changeset `.changeset/25235-missed-scheduled-run.md`: `@objectstack/trigger-schedule`, `@objectstack/service-automation`, `@objectstack/service-job`, each `patch` — one per touched published package, the three packages the diff moves. `Clause-②: yes (widening)` and `Metadata-protocol: none`, line-initial, in both the changeset body and the PR body, identical. **Matches what the diff publishes:** every change above is additive (new methods, optional interface members, barrel types, one more stored option); nothing an author writes changes (no spec key, no accepted value, no metadata type — `Metadata-protocol: none` is right), and nothing accepted before is refused (no `(narrowing)` arm, no `!`, no BREAKING banner, right). Level per AGENTS.md Post-Task Checklist 3: "`none` takes `patch`; a non-protocol change, widening or breaking, ships `patch`" — `patch` ×3 is the prescribed level (ruling item 4 says the same). Title `feat(trigger-schedule): …`, no `!`. `Check Changeset` on the head: success.

`Clause-②:` line judged right: the claim `6433183891` declared `no` and asked for the measurement on the diff; the dev measured `yes (widening)` and recorded the deviation in the os-dev-report. The diff adds public surface on three published packages and one stored status option a reader can receive and filter on, so `yes (widening)` is the true reading (the first claim `6353512245` and the ruling read it the same way). That line alone is what owes this declaration-face review.

### ③ Boundary flags

`open_questions`: `[]` — none to answer.

Dev flags (`out_of_scope_findings` in `6434107183`, and the PR's acceptance notes), each answered or escalated:

1. **Two replicas ticking at once** — a replica that binds in the gap between a due time and the ticking replica's ledger claim records that due time `missed` while the other runs it. Read in the code: real, sub-second, bounded by the ledger check that is the ruling's own verdict source; single-kernel hosted environments (cloud#3149's case) cannot hit it. Same shape at one kernel: a due time exactly at the bind second is recorded by `recordSilence` and may also be fired by the new kernel — the `missed` row and a `completed` row for one due time. **Answered: not a contract breach, carried in the PR's acceptance notes; nothing to escalate under this ruling.** A reader who wants it closed gets a card of its own.
2. **Console reader (ruling item 8).** The dev read `ui/packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/previews/FlowRunsPanel.tsx` at the head (exists in this repo; `STATUS_META` maps five statuses, `statusMeta()` falls back to the raw string with a clock icon), so `missed` renders as the label `missed` with no duration — pass-through, as `timed_out` and `refused` already are. **Answered for `ui/`.** ⛔ Item 8's own instruction is a grep of `../objectui` at the pinned `.objectui-sha` by `domain:server` seat 1 at ACCEPT; that read is the seat's, not this record's, and a closed map there is one `domain:ui` card with `Blocked-by: objectstack-ai/objectstack#25235`. **Escalated to the seat at ACCEPT** (as the dev's carrier line says).
3. **Ruling item 5(g), maintainer question** — whether `missed` rows take a bound tighter than the store's per-flow cap so real history survives a long outage. This PR uses the store's cap, as ruled; one word sets a smaller bound and `missedRunLimit()` is the one place to read it. **Escalated to the maintainer, not blocking, exactly as the ruling flagged it.**

Reviewer's own flags, none blocking:

4. **Release on every policy-OFF pass.** With scheduled work off (the default state of every deployment) and a job service present, each arm pass of a scheduled flow now issues one `sys_job` find (+ an update when a row is active) per flow. `setActive` returns on no row and the cron adapter's `cancel` of an unknown job is a no-op, so there is no warn noise; cost is one read per flow per bind pass. Inside the ruled fix; noted.
5. **Heterogeneous policies on a shared `sys_job` table** — a policy-OFF replica now flips a row an ON replica armed to `inactive`. Nothing in the fire path reads `active` (only `readArming` does, at the head), so the ON replica keeps ticking; the next kernel then reads "not armed" and loses a `missed` entry — the loss direction, never an invention. Noted.
6. **Check-runs on the head at review time (2026-10-27T05:05Z):** 28 completed/success (Check Changeset, Governed Surface Queue Guard, both single-writer and same-issue claim guards, "The card this PR closes must claim this branch", Lint · ESLint, Type Check · source/consumer/workspace/debt ledger, Build Core, Lint & Repo Gates, TypeScript Type Check, Test Core 8/8, Dogfood Regression Gate, Plan Test Core shards, filter, Auto Label, Check PR Size, Flag docs affected, Part-of guard, the scoped lint lanes); 11 completed/skipped (UI, docs, dogfood shards, temporal, opt-in harnesses — none claims a path of this diff); **7 still running: Test Core (1/8) through (7/8).** No check-run has failed. The gate verdicts that have concluded are PASS; the seven shards still in progress are recorded as such and are the merge queue's to finish — this record does not claim them.
7. **PR is a draft.** Ready-for-review is the seat's stroke after the shards land; not a contract point.
